title: Count nested creature mechanics in gameplay-readiness report
description:
`reports/gameplay-readiness.json` in the 2026-06-30 SRD audit bundle undercounts creature mechanics projections because `buildGameplayReadinessReport` only checks top-level `data.mechanics`, `data.projection`, `data.traits[].mechanics`, and `data.feature.mechanics`.

Confirmed bundle: `/home/jhbongaarts/src/dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle-0630-1.zip`, extracted to `/tmp/eshyra-audit-bundle-0630-1`.

Observed:
- `reports/gameplay-readiness.json` reports `byKind.creature.recordsWithMechanicsProjections: 100`.
- A direct scan of creature `traits`, `actions`, `reactions`, and `legendaryActions.entries` finds 314 creature records with nested `mechanics` objects.
- Existing audit docs/reporting elsewhere use the 314/317 creature mechanics count, so this report is inconsistent and understates deterministic gameplay readiness for creatures.

Relevant code: `packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts`, especially `hasMechanicsProjection` and `buildGameplayReadinessReport`.

Acceptance criteria:
- `gameplay-readiness` counts nested mechanics in creature actions, reactions, legendary actions, and traits consistently with the mechanics projection audit.
- Add a regression assertion for the creature mechanics count or for representative nested action/reaction/legendary-action mechanics.
- The report distinguishes top-level record mechanics from nested gameplay mechanics if both signals remain useful.
close_reason: hasMechanicsProjection now also checks nested actions/reactions/legendaryActions.entries; gameplay-readiness now correctly reports creature: 314/317 matching the documented mechanics-projection audit
